title: Fixed finite-stage exceptional adjunction and coefficient interfaces
statement: For the actual finite coefficient stages of [def-coef-finite-coefficient-stages] and a compactification, retain the fixed constructible-finite-Tor derived categories, the etale exceptional adjoint transported through site comparison, and the restricted functors. AdjointDatum records their preservation and adjunction with its specified geometric counit. Change records tensor preservation, the specified normalized projection isomorphism and its counit-transpose mate and unit equation. RefinementDatum records specified lower compactification refinement and its adjoint conjugate. System bundles these data with scalar identity, composition, and refinement equations. These are the existing interfaces, relocated verbatim into an importable data module; the stage and arrow definitions and the two arithmetic stage theorems relocated with them remain owned by their own nodes [def-coef-finite-coefficient-stages, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

source.place: Parent lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons, numbered proof steps; general separated finite-type extension via ordinary-etale closed support as recorded there.

proof.text: The definitions are constructions: the derived categories, the ctf property, scalar extension, the site comparisons, compact support for the given compactification, the etale exceptional right adjoint and its adjunction, the transported right adjoint, the restricted functors, and the records AdjointDatum, Change, RefinementDatum, System and FiniteTypeSystem with their specified normalizations.

etaleLeftAdjoint: the proper map of the compactification is of finite type over the Noetherian target, so the etale adjoint-existence theorem applies to this compactification and these finite coefficients.

finiteTypeNoetherian and finiteTypeMorphismProperties: Spec k is Noetherian, so a scheme locally of finite type and quasi-compact over it is Noetherian. A k-morphism f composed with the target structure map is the source structure map; separatedness and local finite type descend from that composite, and f is quasi-compact because its source is quasi-compact and its target quasi-separated.

proof_origin.place: Stage-3 extraction of the parent argument; normalization uniqueness is by extensionality and injectivity of adjunction transposes.
